The U.S. military said it struck Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets, including air-defense systems, radar sites, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications facilities.
"The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members," CENTCOM said.
The strikes came after a weekend exchange of fire, the first since July.
They also followed Monday attacks on two tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz, a key global oil-shipping route that Iran has effectively closed to commercial traffic.
Iran responded with missile and drone attacks targeting U.S. forces in Jordan, Bahrain and Iraq, Reuters reported.
Jordan said its air defenses intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles that entered its airspace, while Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian drones.
Trump warned Tehran against further retaliation, saying any further response would prompt a "much harder" attack.
